category: TCP/HTTP load balancer (C, event-driven, multi-threaded); the reference L4/L7 balancer
notes: Official HAProxy LTS image (3.4.4): QUIC/HTTP/3 through OpenSSL 3.5's native QUIC API, ACME client (experimental, crt-store starts with a temporary key pair until Pebble issues the certificate), Lua forward-auth through the internal httpclient, jwt_verify for JWTs, stick-tables for rate/connection limits, bwlim filter, built-in cache and Prometheus exporter. Master-worker mode makes `kill -USR2 1` a seamless reload. No UDP, no mirroring, no purge, gzip only.

unsupported.udp_l4: HAProxy proxies TCP and QUIC only; there is no generic UDP proxying (only syslog/DNS forwarding)
unsupported.lb_mirror: no native request mirroring; use tcp-level tee or SPOE + an external agent
unsupported.cache_purge: the built-in cache is a small-object accelerator without an invalidation API; entries expire by max-age (or reload)
unsupported.cache_stale_on_error: the cache has no stale-if-error / grace mode; an expired entry is refetched and the origin's 503 is returned
unsupported.compress_brotli: compression uses libslz (gzip/deflate only); no brotli or zstd support
unsupported.tracing_otel: no OpenTelemetry exporter in the official build (the OpenTracing filter needs a separate addon build)
unsupported.docker_label_discovery: no Docker provider; the Data Plane API / Ingress Controller do this in other setups
